# Policy rules

One versioned bundle (`policy/VERSION`) runs in three places: the IDE (the VS Code extension), pre-commit
(`policy/run-checks.sh --fast`) and CI (the gate that can't be skipped). Every failure names a rule ID, the reason
and the fix. Exceptions go in `waivers.yaml` (approved, time-boxed). Inline `nosem` suppressions are not accepted.

## Code

### <a id="ent-001"></a>ENT-001: No direct provider chat models

**Why:** All LLM traffic must pass the gateway for routing, guardrails, audit and key custody.

**Fix:** Get the model with `get_model()` from `ent_agent_sdk.models`: it uses the model listed under `models:` in `agent.yaml`, so the name is not repeated in code.

```text
# bad
llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-5")

# good
llm = get_model()   # the model comes from agent.yaml
```

### <a id="ent-002"></a>ENT-002: No raw provider clients (`openai`, `anthropic`, `bedrock-runtime`)

**Why:** Same as ENT-001: a raw client bypasses the gateway.

**Fix:** Use `get_model(...)`; call tools and APIs through registered tools.

```text
# bad
client = openai.OpenAI()

# good
llm = get_model()   # the model comes from agent.yaml
```

### <a id="ent-003"></a>ENT-003: No hard-coded provider URLs

**Why:** A provider URL in code is a bypass of the gateway and a place for keys to leak.

**Fix:** Remove it. The SDK knows the gateway URL (`ENT_MODEL_GATEWAY_URL`).

```text
# bad
URL = "https://api.openai.com/v1"

# good
# nothing: use get_model(...)
```

### <a id="ent-004"></a>ENT-004: No credentials read from environment variables

**Why:** Secrets must not live in config or the process environment.

**Fix:** Fetch them at runtime with `secrets.get("name")`.

```text
# bad
key = os.environ["CRM_API_KEY"]

# good
key = secrets.get("crm/api", key="api_key")
```

### <a id="ent-005"></a>ENT-005: No direct Secrets Manager / SSM calls

**Why:** The SDK adds caching, timeouts and fail-closed behaviour.

**Fix:** Use `secrets.get("name")` or `secrets.get("ssm:/path")`.

```text
# bad
boto3.client("secretsmanager").get_secret_value(SecretId="x")

# good
secrets.get("x")
```

### <a id="ent-006"></a>ENT-006: No own web server (`uvicorn.run`, `FastAPI`, `Flask`)

**Why:** The AgentCore contract, tracing, guardrails and health live in the SDK.

**Fix:** Create `EnterpriseAgentApp` (usually `from_manifest`) and call `.run()`.

```text
# bad
app = FastAPI()

# good
app = EnterpriseAgentApp.from_manifest(graph, "agent.yaml")
```

### <a id="ent-007"></a>ENT-007: No raw LangChain `@tool`

**Why:** Tools need an owner, classification, guardrails, audit, timeouts and approval.

**Fix:** Declare tools with `@tools.tool(owner=..., data_classification=...)`.

```text
# bad
from langchain_core.tools import tool

# good
from ent_agent_sdk import tools
```

### <a id="ent-008"></a>ENT-008: Disabling guardrails needs a waiver (warning)

**Why:** Turning guardrails off is a security exception.

**Fix:** Remove it, or add an approved waiver in `waivers.yaml` and reference its ID.

**Exceptions:** allowed only with an approved, unexpired waiver in `waivers.yaml`.

```text
# bad
Guardrails.off(waiver='')

# good
Guardrails.off(waiver="WAIVER-2026-014")  # approved in waivers.yaml
```

### <a id="ent-009"></a>ENT-009: Switching off tool approval needs a waiver (warning)

**Why:** Tools with side effects pause for human approval by default; skipping it is a security exception.

**Fix:** Keep the default, or add an approved ENT-009 waiver and reference it.

**Exceptions:** allowed only with an approved, unexpired waiver in `waivers.yaml`.

```text
# bad
@tools.tool(owner='a', side_effects=True, requires_approval=False, approval_waiver='W-1')

# good
@tools.tool(owner='a', side_effects=True)  # pauses for approval
```

## Dependencies

### <a id="ent-010"></a>ENT-010: `ent-agent-sdk` is required

**Why:** The SDK carries the standards (tracing, guardrails, secrets, gateway access).

**Fix:** Add `"ent-agent-sdk"` to `[project] dependencies`.

```text
# bad
dependencies = ["requests"]

# good
dependencies = ["ent-agent-sdk", "requests"]
```

### <a id="ent-011"></a>ENT-011: No direct `langchain*`, `langgraph*`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `boto3`

**Why:** The SDK pins the approved versions; a direct pin can conflict or bypass them.

**Fix:** Remove it from pyproject.toml; import what you need through the SDK's environment.

```text
# bad
dependencies = ["ent-agent-sdk", "langchain-core>=1"]

# good
dependencies = ["ent-agent-sdk"]
```

### <a id="ent-012"></a>ENT-012: Other dependencies must be on the approved list

**Why:** Every dependency is supply-chain risk and needs review.

**Fix:** Request approval from the platform team (`policy/data/approved-dependencies.json`).

```text
# bad
dependencies = ["ent-agent-sdk", "leftpad"]

# good
dependencies = ["ent-agent-sdk", "httpx"]
```

## Manifest

### <a id="ent-020"></a>ENT-020: `name`, `team` and a valid `data_classification` are required

**Why:** Ownership and data sensitivity drive routing, guardrails and audit.

**Fix:** Fill them in `agent.yaml`.

```text
# bad
name: a

# good
name: crm-agent
team: sales
data_classification: internal
```

### <a id="ent-021"></a>ENT-021: `restricted` data requires `guardrail_profile: strict`

**Why:** Restricted data must never get the lenient profile.

**Fix:** Set `guardrail_profile: strict`.

```text
# bad
data_classification: restricted
guardrail_profile: standard

# good
data_classification: restricted
guardrail_profile: strict
```

### <a id="ent-022"></a>ENT-022: Models must be in the approved registry

**Why:** Only reviewed models may be used.

**Fix:** Use a logical name from `policy/data/approved-models.json`.

```text
# bad
models: [gpt-9]

# good
models: [chat-default]
```

### <a id="ent-023"></a>ENT-023: Restricted agents may only use models approved for restricted data

**Why:** Not every approved model is cleared for restricted data.

**Fix:** Pick a model listed under `restricted_models`.

```text
# bad
data_classification: restricted
models: [chat-fast]

# good
data_classification: restricted
models: [chat-default]
```

## Waivers and pipeline

### <a id="ent-030"></a>ENT-030: Every waiver needs `id`, `rule`, `reason`, `approver`, `expires`

**Why:** Exceptions must be approved and time-boxed.

**Fix:** Complete the waiver entry.

```text
# bad
- id: W-1
  rule: ENT-008

# good
- id: W-1
  rule: ENT-008
  reason: eval
  approver: a@b.com
  expires: 2026-12-31
```

### <a id="ent-031"></a>ENT-031: Expired waivers fail the build

**Why:** Exceptions must end.

**Fix:** Fix the code, or renew the waiver with a new approval.

```text
# bad
expires: 2026-01-01

# good
expires: 2026-12-31
```

### <a id="ent-032"></a>ENT-032: Waiver references in code must be approved and unexpired

**Why:** `Guardrails.off(waiver=...)` / `approval_waiver=...` must name a real waiver for the right rule (ENT-008 / ENT-009).

**Fix:** Add the approved waiver to `waivers.yaml`, or remove the exception.

```text
# bad
Guardrails.off(waiver="W-404")

# good
# W-404 exists in waivers.yaml, rule ENT-008, not expired
```

### <a id="ent-033"></a>ENT-033: No inline `nosem` suppressions

**Why:** Suppressions hide violations from review.

**Fix:** Use `waivers.yaml`.

```text
# bad
llm = ChatOpenAI()  # nosem

# good
# fix the code, or add a waiver
```

### <a id="ent-040"></a>ENT-040: CI must call the platform pipeline

**Why:** The gates only protect repos that run them.

**Fix:** Call `agent-ci.yml@<tag>` from `.github/workflows`.

```text
# bad
# custom pipeline

# good
uses: org/platform2.0/.github/workflows/agent-ci.yml@v0.1.0
```

### <a id="ent-041"></a>ENT-041: Pin the pipeline to a release tag or commit SHA

**Why:** A branch can change under you.

**Fix:** Use a tag like `@v0.1.0` or a SHA.

```text
# bad
uses: org/platform2.0/.github/workflows/agent-ci.yml@main

# good
uses: org/platform2.0/.github/workflows/agent-ci.yml@v0.1.0
```

### <a id="ent-042"></a>ENT-042: The pipeline job can't be conditional or allowed to fail

**Why:** A skippable gate is not a gate.

**Fix:** Remove `if:` and `continue-on-error`.

```text
# bad
if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'

# good
# no condition
```

### <a id="ent-043"></a>ENT-043: CI must run on pull requests

**Why:** Problems must be caught before merge.

**Fix:** Add `pull_request` to `on:`.

```text
# bad
on: [push]

# good
on: [push, pull_request]
```

### <a id="ent-060"></a>ENT-060: Release past its sunset or no longer supported

**Why:** Old SDK and policy releases stop getting fixes; after the sunset date the build fails (N-1 support, 90-day sunset).

**Fix:** Upgrade `ent-agent-sdk` / the pipeline tag to a supported release (see `policy/data/versions.json`).

```text
# bad
uses: org/platform2.0/.github/workflows/agent-ci.yml@v0.1.0   # sunset 2027-01-01, today is later

# good
uses: org/platform2.0/.github/workflows/agent-ci.yml@v0.2.0
```

### <a id="ent-061"></a>ENT-061: Release sunsets soon (warning)

**Why:** Plan the upgrade before the sunset date turns this into a build failure.

**Fix:** Upgrade to the latest release.

```text
# bad
ent-agent-sdk 0.1.x with a sunset in 30 days

# good
ent-agent-sdk 0.2.x
```

### <a id="ent-062"></a>ENT-062: Could not determine the SDK or pipeline version (warning)

**Why:** The deprecation check needs `uv.lock` (or a pinned `ent-agent-sdk`) and a pinned pipeline tag.

**Fix:** Commit `uv.lock` and call the pipeline with a tag.

```text
# bad
no uv.lock, unpinned dependency

# good
uv.lock committed
```

### <a id="ent-050"></a>ENT-050: Dependency licences must not match denied patterns

**Why:** Some licences (AGPL, SSPL, non-commercial) are incompatible with our use.

**Fix:** Replace the dependency or get a licence exception.

```text
# bad
a dependency licensed AGPL-3.0

# good
an MIT / BSD / Apache-2.0 dependency
```

## Other gates (in the pipeline, `.github/workflows/agent-ci.yml`)

Secret scanning (gitleaks), dependency vulnerabilities (pip-audit) and SAST (Semgrep) with severity thresholds,
SBOM (CycloneDX) and licence check, unit tests and local-runtime integration tests in replay mode, the evaluation
gate (golden questions with minimum scores), SDK/policy version support (deprecation) and image signing.
